plan.title: Colon RSEM: treated vs control DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: 12000-gene x 12-sample RSEM gene-level expected-count matrix (colon, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) lacks the per-sample genes.results files, so the effective-length offset that RSEM/tximport normally supplies cannot be reconstructed — the matrix is the only input available. Track 1 runs the DESeq2 path directly on this matrix: sample-structure QC first (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library-size/detected-gene table) to inspect sample_01 (library size ~4x below the median) without deleting it by default; minimal low-count pre-filtering; DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization and Wald test with an explicit reference level (control); apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control coefficient; BH-adjusted results with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, and a p-value histogram check. An edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design runs in parallel as the robustness cross-check the DE step recommends at 6-per-group replication, and the report treats the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence gene set. Track 2 takes the DESeq2 Wald statistic ranking into fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome + WikiPathways (follow-up, both staged for human), all mapped through org.Hs.eg.db with the unmapped share reported. A final report step assembles the DE table (unshrunken and shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, padj), the two fit diagnostic plots, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and the full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions, seeds). Caveat carried throughout: RSEM expected counts are not integers and effective-length offsets are missing, so DESeq2's counts are rounded to integers as a documented deviation from the ideal tximport-mediated import — this is flagged in the report rather than silently done.
